questions.question: A thief escaped with a bike, riding at the speed of 70 km/h. A policeman arrived at the spot of the theft an hour after the bike was stolen and started chasing the thief. If the policeman drove his vehicle at the speed of 84 km/h, for how many hours did the policeman have to drive before catching the thief?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of the thief = 70 km/h.

Speed of the policeman = 84 km/h.

The policeman started chasing after 1 hour.

**Formula Used:**

Time taken by the policeman to catch the thief = Distance / Relative Speed

**Calculation:**

Distance covered by the thief in 1 hour = 70 km

Relative Speed = Speed of the policeman - Speed of the thief

Relative Speed = 84 km/h - 70 km/h = 14 km/h

Time taken by the policeman to catch the thief = Distance / Relative Speed

⇒ Time taken by the policeman to catch the thief = 70 km / 14 km/h

⇒ Time taken by the policeman to catch the thief = 5 hours

**The policeman had to drive for 5 hours before catching the thief.**

questions.question: An aeroplane covers a distance at a speed of 190 km/h in 7 hours. To cover the distance in 4(3)/(4) hours, it must travel at a speed (in km/h) of:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When distance is constant, Speed ∝ 1 / Time

Ratio of Time = T₁ : T₂ = 7 : 19/4 = 28 : 19

Ratio of Speed = S₁ : S₂ = 19 : 28

Given 19 units = 190 km/h ⇒ 1 unit = 10 km/h

Required Speed = 28 units = 280 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 280 km/h.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial speed = 190 km/h

Initial time = 7 hours

New time = 4(3/4) hours = 19/4 hours

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

New Speed = Total Distance ÷ New Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3aec8f6505c48531e21d4f90d7372f35af499997087a30dcf564dd02bbf7b547.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 190 × 7 = 1330 km

⇒ New Speed = Total Distance ÷ New Time

⇒ New Speed = 1330 ÷ (19/4)

⇒ New Speed = 1330 × (4 / 19)

⇒ New Speed = 70 × 4 = 280 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 280 km/h.**

**__Additional Information__**

Speed, Distance & Time Relationship

Distance = Speed × Time. For a constant distance, speed is inversely proportional to time (S ∝ 1 / T).

Unit Conversions

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Average Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. If two equal distances are covered at speeds a and b, Average Speed = (2ab) ÷ (a + b).
</p

questions.question: A bus covers a distance of 45 km in 45 minutes. If its speed is decreased by 20 km/hr, then what will be the time taken by it to cover the same distance?
questions.solution:
**Given Data:**

Distance = 45 km

Initial time = 45 minutes

Speed decreased by 20 km/hr

**Concept: **Time = Distance/Speed

**Solution:**

⇒ Initial speed = Distance/time = 45 km/(45 min/60) hr = 60 km/hr

⇒ Reduced speed = Initial speed - reduction = 60 km/hr - 20 km/hr = 40 km/hr

⇒ New time = Distance/Reduced speed = 45 km/40 km/hr = 1.125 hr = 67.5 min

**Therefore, the new time taken to cover the same distance is 67.5 minutes.**

questions.question: A train covers a distance of 54 km from station A to station G in an hour via stations B, C, D, E and F. On each station, the train stops for 72 seconds. What is the speed of the train in km / h?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The train covers a distance of 54 km from station A to station G in an hour, stopping at stations B, C, D, E, and F for 72 seconds each.

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Total distance / Total time taken

**Calculation:**

Time taken for stops:

There are 5 stops, each for 72 seconds.

Total stopping time = 5 × 72 seconds

Total stopping time = 360 seconds

Total stopping time in hours = 360 / 3600

Total stopping time in hours = 0.1 hours

Total time taken to cover the distance:

Total travel time = 1 hour - 0.1 hour

Total travel time = 0.9 hours

Speed of the train:

Distance = 54 km

Time = 0.9 hours

Speed = Distance / Time

Speed = 54 / 0.9

Speed = 60 km/h

**The speed of the train is 60 km/h.**

questions.question: P and Q start from point A to point B, at the same time at speeds of 32 km/h and 40 km/h, respectively. If in covering the journey P takes 15 minutes longer than Q, the total distance AB of the journey is:

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct Formula for Distance

If two speeds are S₁ and S₂ and the absolute time difference is Δt, then Distance = [(S₁ × S₂) ÷ |S₁ − S₂|] × Δt.

Average Speed

If a certain distance is covered at speed x and the same distance is covered at speed y, then the Average Speed for the entire journey = (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).

questions.question: From point P, X walks at a speed of 12 km/hr and 6 hours after his start Y also starts walking from same point P on his cycle after him at the speed of 16 km/hr. How far from the starting point P will Y catch X?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

X's speed = 12 km/hr

Y's speed = 16 km/hr

Time difference between X's and Y's start = 6 hours

**Concept:**

When Y starts, X has already covered a certain distance. Y will catch up by covering the distance X has covered plus the additional distance at a relative speed.

**Formula Used:**

Distance covered = Speed × Time

Relative speed = Speed of Y - Speed of X

**Calculation:**

Distance covered by X in 6 hours:

⇒ DistanceX = 12 km/hr × 6 hr

⇒ DistanceX = 72 km

Relative speed of Y catching up to X:

⇒ Relative speed = 16 km/hr - 12 km/hr

⇒ Relative speed = 4 km/hr

Time taken by Y to catch up to X:

⇒ Time = DistanceX / Relative speed

⇒ Time = 72 km / 4 km/hr

⇒ Time = 18 hours

Distance from starting point P when Y catches X:

⇒ Distance = SpeedY × Total time

⇒ Distance = 16 km/hr × (18 hours)

⇒ Distance = 288 km

**∴ The correct answer is option 2 (288 km).**

questions.question: Two places A and B are 60 km apart from each other on a highway. A car starts from A and another car from B at the same time. If they move in the same direction, they meet each other in 6 hours, If they move in the opposite direction towards each other, they meet in 1 hour 30 minutes. Find the speeds of the cars (in km/h).
questions.solution:
**Formula Used:**

When moving in the same direction, relative speed = |v₁ - v₂|

When moving in the opposite direction, relative speed = v₁ + v₂

Where v₁ and v₂ are the speeds of the two cars.

**Calculation:**

Let the speed of the car starting from A be v₁ km/h and the speed of the car starting from B be v₂ km/h.

**1. When moving in the same direction:**

⇒ Distance = Relative speed × Time

⇒ 60 km = |v₁ - v₂| × 6 hours

⇒ |v₁ - v₂| = 60 km / 6 hours

⇒ |v₁ - v₂| = 10 km/h ...(1)

**2. When moving in opposite directions:**

⇒ Distance = Relative speed × Time

⇒ 60 km = (v₁ + v₂) × 1.5 hours

⇒ v₁ + v₂ = 60 km / 1.5 hours

⇒ v₁ + v₂ = 40 km/h ...(2)

From equations (1) and (2):

⇒ v₁ - v₂ = 10 km/h ...(3)

⇒ v₁ + v₂ = 40 km/h ...(4)

Adding equations (3) and (4):

⇒ 2v₁ = 50 km/h

⇒ v₁ = 25 km/h

Substituting v₁ = 25 km/h into equation (4):

⇒ 25 + v₂ = 40

⇒ v₂ = 15 km/h

**∴ The speeds of the cars are 25 km/h and 15 km/h.**

questions.question: A police officer follows a thief who is at a distance of 800 m from him. If they run at a speed of 8 km/h and 7 km/h, respectively, how long does the police officer have to run to catch up with the thief?
questions.solution:

Distance between the thief and the police officer = 800 m

Speed of the police officer = 8 km/h = 8000 m/h

Speed of the thief = 7 km/h = 7000 m/h

⇒ Relative speed of the police officer with respect to the thief = 8000 - 7000 = 1000 m/h

⇒ Time required to catch up with the thief = Distance/Relative speed = 800/(1000/3600) = 2880 seconds = 0.8 hours

⇒ Distance covered by the police officer = Speed × Time = 8000 × 0.8 = 6400 m

**Hence, the police officer has to run 6400 m to catch up with the thief.**

questions.question: A thief seeing a policeman from a distance of 550 metres started running at a speed of 9 km/h. The policeman began to chase him immediately, at a speed of 11 km/h and the thief was caught. What is the distance run by the thief before he was caught by the policeman?
questions.solution:
**Given:- **Speed of policeman = 11 km/h, speed of thief = 9 km/h, distance between thief and policeman = 550 m

**To find:-** The distance run by the thief before getting caught

**Formula used:- Distance = speed × time**

**Calculations:-** The distance covered by thief before getting caught is distance** 'd' m**

So, the total distance travelled by the policeman = **(550 + d) m**

The total time taken by the policeman to cover (550 + d) and the thief to covered d will be same, let's say **t**

The **speed of policeman** = 11km/h = 11times(5)/(18)m/s , the **speed of thief** = 9km/h = 9times(5)/(18) m/s

⇒Time taken by policeman (**t**) = ((550+d))/((frac{55){18})} = (18times(550+d))/(55) ------------------(i)

⇒Time taken by thief (**t**) = ((d))/((frac{45){18})} = (18d)/(45)--------------------------------------(ii)

**Equating both eq(i) and (ii),**

⇒(18times(550+d))/(55) = (18d)/(45)

⇒9times(550+d)=11times(d)

⇒4950 = 2d

⇒**d = 2475 m**

 

**The distance covered by the thief before getting caught is 2475 metres.**

questions.question: In a 5 km race, X, Y and Z, each running at a uniform speed, get the gold, silver, and bronze medals, respectively. If X beats Y by 0.5 km and Y beats Z by 0.5 km, then by how many metres does X beat Z?
questions.solution:
**Solution:**

In a linear race of 5 km, X beats Y by 0.5 km, while Y beats Z by 0.5 km.

**Calculation:**

X beats Y by 0.5 km

X : Y = 5 : (5 - 0.5) = 5 : 4.5 = 10 : 9 -----(i)

Y beats Z by 0.5 km

Y : Z = 5 : (5 - 0.5) = 5 : 4.5 = 10 : 9 ----- (ii)

From 10 × (i) and 9 × (ii)

X : Y = 100 : 90

Y : Z = 90 : 81

Now, X : Y : Z = 100 : 90 : 81

X : Z = 100 : 81

When X covers 100 km then Z covers = 81 km

X covers 5 then Z covers = (81/100) × 5 = 4.05 km

X will beat Z in a race of 5000 m = 5000 - 4050 = 950 m

The answer is 950 m.

questions.question: Two friends are running on a circular track of 720 m. They started from the same point and are moving in the same direction with speeds of 1.5 m/s and 3.5 m/s. After how much time will they cross each other for the second time?
questions.solution:
**Given data:**

Circular track length = 720 m, speeds = 1.5 m/s and 3.5 m/s

**Concept:**

Relative speed concept in circular track.

They meet for the second time when they cover a distance of 2 times the track length.

**Solution:**

Relative speed = 3.5 m/s - 1.5 m/s = 2 m/s

Time taken to meet for the second time = 2 × 720 m / 2 m/s = 720 seconds = 12 minutes

**Therefore, they will cross each other for the second time after 12 minutes.**

questions.question: A thief is observed by a policeman from a distance of 420 m. The thief starts running and the policeman chases him. The policeman and the thief run at a speed of 25 km/h and 20 km/h, respectively. What is the distance between them after three minutes?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Initial distance = 420 m

Policeman's speed = 25 km/h

Thief's speed = 20 km/h

Time = 3 min

**Concept:**

Relative speed and distance = speed × time

Solution:

⇒ Convert speeds from km/h to m/min: Policeman's speed = 25 × 1000/60 = 416.67 m/min, Thief's speed = 20 × 1000/60 = 333.33 m/min

⇒ Relative speed = 416.67 m/min - 333.33 m/min = 83.33 m/min

⇒ Distance covered in 3 min = 83.33 m/min × 3 min = 250 m

⇒ Remaining distance = 420 m - 250 m = 170 m

**Therefore, the distance between them after three minutes is 170 m.**

questions.question: In a circular race of 5000 m, starting from the same point, the speeds of two contestants A and B are 36 km/h and 54 km/h, respectively. The difference between the time taken (in seconds) to meet for the first time when they are running in the opposite directions and when they are running in the same direction?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Circular race length: 5000 m

Speed of A: 36 km/h (or 10 m/s)

Speed of B: 54 km/h (or 15 m/s)

**Concept:**

Time = Distance/Speed. In opposite directions, the speeds add up; in the same direction, they subtract.

**Solution:**

Time taken when running in opposite directions = 5000/(10 + 15) ⇒ 200 seconds

Time taken when running in the same direction = 5000/(15 - 10) ⇒ 1000 seconds

The difference in times = 1000 - 200 ⇒ 800 seconds

**Therefore, the difference between the times taken to meet for the first time in opposite and the same directions is 800 seconds.**

questions.question: Two cyclists start at the same time from opposite ends of a 200 km long straight road. One cyclist travels at a speed of 20 km/h and the other at a speed of 30 km/h. How long will it take them to meet?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two moving bodies travel in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds.

Relative Speed = 20 + 30 = 50 km/h

Time = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Time = 200 ÷ 50 = 4 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 4 hours.**

Total distance between the two cyclists (D) = 200 km

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (when moving in opposite directions) = S₁ + S₂

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 20 km/h + 30 km/h

⇒ Relative Speed = 50 km/h

⇒ Time taken to meet = 200 km ÷ 50 km/h

⇒ Time taken = 4 hours

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Opposite Directions)

When two bodies move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: SR = S₁ + S₂.

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their individual speeds: SR = |S₁ − S₂|.

Average Speed

When a journey involves different speeds, the Average Speed over the entire journey is given by: Total Distance ÷ Total Time.

questions.question: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 108 m. The thief starts running and the policeman chases him. If the speed of the thief and policeman are 21 km/h and 23 km/h, respectively, then how far will the thief have to run (in m) before he is overtaken by the policeman?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance between the thief and policeman = 108 m.

Speed of the thief = 21 km/h.

Speed of the policeman = 23 km/h.

**Formula Used:**

Relative speed = Speed of policeman - Speed of thief

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculation:**

First, convert speeds from km/h to m/s by multiplying with (5)/(18) .

Speed of the thief in m/s = 21 × (5)/(18) 

Speed of the policeman in m/s = 23 × (5)/(18) 

Relative speed in m/s = (23 - 21) × (5)/(18) 

Relative speed in m/s = 2 × (5)/(18) 

Relative speed in m/s = (10)/(18) m/s

Distance to be covered to catch the thief = Initial distance = 108 m

Time to catch the thief = Distance / Relative speed

⇒ Time = 108 / (10)/(18) 

⇒ Time = 108 × (18)/(10) 

Distance run by the thief = Speed of thief in m/s × Time

⇒ Distance = 21 × 5/18 × 18/10 × 108 = 1134

**The thief will have to run 1134 m before he is overtaken by the policeman.**

questions.question: A thief is noticed by a policeman from a distance of 150 m. The thief starts running and the policeman chases him. The thief and policeman run at the speed of 11km/h and 12km/h, respectively. What is the distance between them after 6 minutes?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Initial distance = 150 m,

Speed of thief = 11 km/hr,

Speed of policeman = 12 km/hr,

Time = 6 min

**Concept:**

Relative speed is the speed of one object as observed from the other,

which is the difference in their speeds.

Distance = Speed × Time

**Steps:**

Convert speeds from km/hr to m/min:

Speed of thief = 11 × 1000/60

⇒ 183.33 m/min,

Speed of policeman = 12 × 1000/60

⇒ 200 m/min

Relative speed = Speed of policeman - Speed of thief

⇒ 200 - 183.33 = 16.67 m/min

Distance covered by a policeman in 6 min

⇒ Relative speed × Time = 16.67 × 6 = 100 m

Final distance between thief and policeman = Initial distance - Distance covered by a policeman

⇒ 150 - 100 = 50 m

**Therefore, the distance between the thief and the policeman after 6 minutes is 50 m.**
